    child_pid, fd = pty.fork()

rules.name: vuln-next-react2shell
rules.message: This Next.js version is vulnerable to React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182 / CVE-2025-66478).
rules.why: Unauthenticated RCE via insecure deserialisation of the RSC Flight reply — a __proto__/constructor gadget reaches the Function constructor and runs OS commands. No app code is needed; a static app is affected.

rules.name: weak-cipher
rules.message: This is a weak or ECB-mode cipher.
rules.remediation: Use AES-GCM (or another authenticated mode) with a random nonce.
rules.why: DES/RC4 are broken, and ECB leaks structure because equal blocks encrypt equally.

rules.name: weak-hash
rules.message: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security use.
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256+ for integrity, and bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 for passwords.
rules.why: Both have practical collisions and are far too fast for password hashing.

rules.name: weak-hash-md5-sha1-token-js
rules.message: Predictable session/token identifier — a security id from a non-CSPRNG or observable source (CWE-330/340).
rules.remediation: Generate the identifier from a CSPRNG (crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex') or crypto.randomUUID()); never derive a security token by hashing user-known or observable data with md5/sha1.
rules.why: A session id or token built by md5/sha1-hashing a known or low-entropy value (username, email, IP, timestamp) is fully predictable: the hash adds no entropy, so an attacker who knows the inputs can recompute the token and hijack the session or forge a reset link.

rules.name: weak-hash-md5-sha1-token-py
rules.message: Predictable session/token identifier — a security id from a non-CSPRNG or observable source (CWE-330/340).
rules.remediation: Generate the identifier with secrets.token_urlsafe/token_hex or os.urandom; do not hash user-known data with md5/sha1 to make a token.
rules.why: A security token produced by hashlib.md5/sha1 over a known value (username, email, user id, timestamp) is predictable because the input is guessable and the hash adds no secrecy; the attacker recomputes it.

rules.name: weak-otp-context-noncrypto-js
rules.message: GraphQL/dev misconfiguration — introspection or a dev endpoint exposed, or a weak/predictable secret (CWE-200/489/307/770/330).
rules.remediation: Use crypto.randomInt() (node:crypto) for the code and gate any dev-only Math.random path behind an explicit env guard if kept at all.
rules.why: An OTP/verification/2FA value on a line that uses Math.random() derives an authentication code from a non-cryptographic RNG, making it predictable regardless of the exact numeric shape.

rules.name: weak-otp-go-mathrand
rules.message: GraphQL/dev misconfiguration — introspection or a dev endpoint exposed, or a weak/predictable secret (CWE-200/489/307/770/330).
rules.remediation: Use crypto/rand (rand.Int with a large modulus, or a CSPRNG helper) for verification codes.
rules.why: An OTP built from math/rand rand.Intn over a small range is predictable and seedable, so codes can be recovered or guessed.

rules.name: weak-otp-java-kotlin-csharp-random
rules.message: GraphQL/dev misconfiguration — introspection or a dev endpoint exposed, or a weak/predictable secret (CWE-200/489/307/770/330).
rules.remediation: Use SecureRandom (Java/Kotlin) or RandomNumberGenerator.GetInt32 (.NET) for verification codes.
rules.why: An OTP from java.util.Random / Kotlin Random / System.Random over a small range is predictable and its seed/internal state can be recovered from a few outputs.

rules.name: weak-otp-math-random-numeric-shape
rules.message: GraphQL/dev misconfiguration — introspection or a dev endpoint exposed, or a weak/predictable secret (CWE-200/489/307/770/330).
rules.remediation: Generate OTPs with crypto.randomInt(min, max) from node:crypto, and add short expiry plus attempt lockout.
rules.why: A verification code / OTP built from Math.random() over a tiny numeric range (4-6 digits) or by slicing digits off the decimal expansion is low-entropy and brute-forceable; Math.random is not a CSPRNG.

rules.name: weak-otp-php-rand
rules.message: GraphQL/dev misconfiguration — introspection or a dev endpoint exposed, or a weak/predictable secret (CWE-200/489/307/770/330).
rules.remediation: Use random_int() (PHP 7+) for verification codes and add attempt throttling.
rules.why: An OTP produced by rand()/mt_rand() (non-CSPRNG) over a 4-6 digit range is predictable and its Mersenne-Twister state can be recovered.

rules.name: weak-otp-python-random
rules.message: GraphQL/dev misconfiguration — introspection or a dev endpoint exposed, or a weak/predictable secret (CWE-200/489/307/770/330).
rules.remediation: Use secrets.randbelow / secrets.choice (or random.SystemRandom) for verification codes and add per-user rate limiting.
rules.why: An OTP/verification code drawn from the non-crypto random module (randint/randrange over a 4-6 digit range, or choice over a digit string) is predictable and, with a recovered seed, reproducible.

rules.name: weak-otp-ruby-rand
rules.message: GraphQL/dev misconfiguration — introspection or a dev endpoint exposed, or a weak/predictable secret (CWE-200/489/307/770/330).
rules.remediation: Use SecureRandom.random_number for verification codes and add attempt lockout.
rules.why: An OTP from Kernel#rand / Random#rand over a small numeric range is predictable and not suitable for authentication codes.

rules.name: weak-password-min-length
rules.message: Password policy allows fewer than 8 characters.
rules.remediation: Require at least 8 (ideally 12+) characters, check candidates against a breached-password list, and prefer passphrases over arbitrary complexity rules.
rules.why: A minimum length below 8 lets users pick trivially guessable passwords and makes offline cracking and credential-stuffing far easier. Length is the single strongest lever on password strength.

rules.name: weak-random-ticks-as-token-cs
rules.message: Predictable session/token identifier — a security id from a non-CSPRNG or observable source (CWE-330/340).
rules.remediation: Use RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes / RandomNumberGenerator.Create (or the legacy RNGCryptoServiceProvider) to produce security tokens; never System.Random or a clock value.
rules.why: System.Random (including Random.Shared) is a non-cryptographic PRNG and DateTime.Now.Ticks / Environment.TickCount are observable clocks; a session id or token built from them is predictable and can be recomputed by an attacker.

rules.name: weak-random-time-as-token-java
rules.message: Predictable session/token identifier — a security id from a non-CSPRNG or observable source (CWE-330/340).
rules.remediation: Use java.security.SecureRandom (or UUID.randomUUID, which is backed by SecureRandom) for session ids and tokens.
rules.why: java.util.Random / Math.random / ThreadLocalRandom are non-cryptographic PRNGs and System.currentTimeMillis / nanoTime are observable clocks; using them to build a session id or token yields a predictable value an attacker can reproduce.

rules.name: weak-url-validation
rules.message: A URL is validated by substring/prefix instead of being parsed.
rules.remediation: Parse with new URL() and compare url.hostname/url.protocol against an explicit allowlist.
rules.why: indexOf("example.com") or startsWith("http") is bypassable: https://evil.com/?example.com and https://example.com.evil.com both pass, opening a redirect or letting a hostile origin through.

rules.name: ws-connection-auth
rules.message: A WebSocket connection handler — verify the client is authenticated.
rules.remediation: Authenticate the connection (a token in the upgrade request / first message) before honouring any action.
rules.why: WebSocket upgrades are not covered by the page's auth by default, so a handler that trusts an in-band action like {action:'AUTH', user:'admin'} without checking a token lets anyone claim any identity.

rules.name: xxe-fast-xml-parser-process-entities
rules.message: XML entity expansion / XXE — an XML parser resolves entities on untrusted input (CWE-776/611).
rules.remediation: Parse untrusted XML with processEntities:false and reject documents containing a <!DOCTYPE>/<!ENTITY>. Do not enable htmlEntities on attacker-controlled input either.
rules.why: fast-xml-parser's XMLParser resolves XML entity references only when processEntities is true; on untrusted input (e.g. parser.parse(req.body.data)) a document can declare recursively nested internal entities that expand exponentially, a billion-laughs denial of service that exhausts memory and CPU. The safe twin processEntities:false, `===` equality checks, the *Enabled/*Default identifier suffixes, and comment lines are all excluded.

rules.name: xxe-java-xml-factory-unhardened
rules.message: XML entity expansion / XXE — an XML parser resolves entities on untrusted input (CWE-776/611).
rules.remediation: Immediately harden the factory: setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true) (or FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING), set ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/ACCESS_EXTERNAL_STYLESHEET to "", and for StAX set XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD and IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES to false.
rules.why: A JAXP/dom4j factory (DocumentBuilderFactory, SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory, TransformerFactory, dom4j SAXReader) created via the no-arg newInstance()/new SAXReader() processes DOCTYPE declarations and external entities by default; unless hardened it lets untrusted XML perform XXE (local file disclosure, SSRF) and entity-expansion DoS. Instances hardened on the same line (disallow-doctype-decl true, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, SUPPORT_DTD false, empty ACCESS_EXTERNAL_*, setExpandEntityReferences(false)) and comment lines are suppressed. Note: the empty-parens anchor means SchemaFactory.newInstance(schemaLang) and string literals do not match; multi-line hardening (harden on a following line) is a known limitation of a single-line regex.

rules.name: xxe-libxmljs-noent-replace-entities
rules.message: XML entity expansion / XXE — an XML parser resolves entities on untrusted input (CWE-776/611).
rules.remediation: Parse untrusted XML with the default noent:false (do not substitute entities); avoid dtdload/dtdvalid unless a DTD is required, and verify no <!ENTITY> declarations are present.
rules.why: libxmljs parseXml/parseXmlString with { noent: true } (XML_PARSE_NOENT) or { replaceEntities: true } substitutes entity references while parsing; an untrusted document can then trigger exponential internal-entity expansion (billion laughs) and, with DTD loading, external-entity injection. The colon-keyed sink deliberately matches the option-object form only, so noent:false / replaceEntities:false twins, `= true` assignments to unrelated vars, *Value/*Enabled suffixes, and comment lines are excluded.

rules.name: xxe-lxml-resolve-entities
rules.message: XML entity expansion / XXE — an XML parser resolves entities on untrusted input (CWE-776/611).
rules.remediation: Construct the parser with resolve_entities=False and no_network=True (and load_dtd=False), or use defusedxml.lxml which disables entity resolution and external access by default.
rules.why: An lxml etree.XMLParser built with resolve_entities=True substitutes entity references (enabling billion-laughs expansion), and no_network=False re-enables network fetches for external entities/DTDs; either makes parsing attacker XML unsafe. The safe twins resolve_entities=False / no_network=True, the *_flag/*_default identifier suffixes, defusedxml.lxml usage, and comment lines are excluded.

rules.name: xxe-php-libxml-noent
rules.message: XML entity expansion / XXE — an XML parser resolves entities on untrusted input (CWE-776/611).
rules.remediation: Do not pass LIBXML_NOENT/LIBXML_DTDLOAD when parsing untrusted XML (the defaults do not expand entities); on PHP < 8 call libxml_disable_entity_loader(true), keep LIBXML_NONET set to block network fetches, and reject documents containing a DOCTYPE.
rules.why: simplexml_load_string/simplexml_load_file/DOMDocument::loadXML on request-controlled input, or any such call passing LIBXML_NOENT / LIBXML_DTDLOAD, substitutes entities and loads DTDs, enabling billion-laughs entity-expansion DoS and, with network access, XXE. A hardened call using LIBXML_NONET without LIBXML_NOENT (negative-lookahead excluded), trusted/literal input with no tainted-var token, loadXMLSchema, and comment lines are all suppressed.

rules.name: xxe-xslt-secure-processing-disabled
rules.message: Renderer resource embedding — a document/PDF/image converter resolves a user-controlled resource, enabling LFI or SSRF (CWE-918/73/611).
rules.remediation: Enable FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING(true), set ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD to "", keep setExpandEntityReferences(false) / SUPPORT_DTD false, and disallow DOCTYPE declarations on untrusted input.
rules.why: Disabling FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, allowing external DTDs, expanding entity references, or supporting DTDs in the XML/XSLT/FO parser lets a user-supplied document declare external entities/DTDs, yielding XXE-based local file disclosure (LFI) and out-of-band internal fetches (SSRF) during conversion. Added \b after true/false so identifiers like trueMode, trueByDefault, falseIfLegacy no longer match.

rules.name: yaml-load
rules.message: yaml.load() can construct arbitrary Python objects.
rules.remediation: Use yaml.safe_load(), or pass Loader=SafeLoader.
rules.why: The default loader instantiates types named in the document, which is remote code execution on untrusted input.

rules.name: yoga-masked-errors-disabled
rules.message: GraphQL/dev misconfiguration — introspection or a dev endpoint exposed, or a weak/predictable secret (CWE-200/489/307/770/330).
rules.remediation: Keep masking on in production. Remove `maskedErrors: false`, or gate it: `maskedErrors: process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`. To customize safely, pass a `maskError` function returning sanitized messages.
rules.why: graphql-yoga masks unexpected errors by default so raw exception messages and stack traces never reach clients. `maskedErrors: false` turns masking off, leaking internal error details (DB errors, stack traces) to every caller. A hardcoded false disables the protection in production. A JS ternary (`isDev ? false : true`) or a variable places the value away from the separator so no literal false immediately follows; case-sensitivity keeps `disableMaskedErrors:` (capital M) from matching.

rules.name: zipslip-csharp-extracttofile-combine
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Build the path then verify: var full = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(dest, entry.FullName)); if (!full.StartsWith(Path.GetFullPath(dest) + Path.DirectorySeparatorChar)) throw. Reject '..'/rooted FullName and skip zero-length symlink-style entries.
rules.why: Per-entry extraction with entry.ExtractToFile / Path.Combine(dir, entry.FullName) uses the untrusted ZipArchiveEntry.FullName; Path.Combine with a rooted or ../-laden FullName resolves outside the destination, so extraction writes an arbitrary file (unlike ZipFile.ExtractToDirectory which validates).

rules.name: zipslip-go-filepathjoin-name
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: After joining, check containment: rel, err := filepath.Rel(dest, target); reject when err != nil or strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."); or require strings.HasPrefix(target, filepath.Clean(dest)+string(os.PathSeparator)). Use EvalSymlinks and skip link headers.
rules.why: filepath.Join(dest, f.Name) / filepath.Join(dest, header.Name) inside a zip.Reader/tar.Reader loop builds the output path from the untrusted entry name; filepath.Join cleans but does not confine, so a ../ prefix escapes dest and the following os.Create/io.Copy writes an arbitrary file.

rules.name: zipslip-java-newfile-getname
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Resolve and canonicalize the target: File f = new File(destDir, name); if (!f.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(destDir.getCanonicalPath()+File.separator)) throw new IOException(). Reject '..' and absolute names; do not follow symlink entries.
rules.why: new File(destDir, zipEntry.getName()) builds the output file directly from the untrusted ZIP/tar entry name; a getName() value such as ../../../opt/app.jar makes the File resolve outside destDir, and the subsequent FileOutputStream/Files.copy performs an arbitrary file write.

rules.name: zipslip-kotlin-file-entryname
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Build the file then verify containment: val f = File(destDir, entry.name); if (!f.canonicalPath.startsWith(destDir.canonicalPath + File.separator)) throw IOException(). Reject '..'/absolute names and skip symlink entries.
rules.why: Kotlin File(destDir, entry.name) constructs the extraction target from the untrusted ZipEntry.name; a traversal name escapes destDir and the following outputStream()/copyTo writes attacker-controlled content to an arbitrary path. A leading word boundary keeps the short 'ze' token from matching inside identifiers like size/maze/blaze.

rules.name: zipslip-node-admzip-extractallto
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Do not call extractAllTo on untrusted archives. Iterate entries and, for each, compute path.resolve(dest, entry.entryName) and confirm it startsWith(path.resolve(dest)+path.sep) before writing; reject absolute names and symlink entries.
rules.why: adm-zip extractAllTo()/extractAllToAsync() writes every entry to disk using the archive-internal entry names; a crafted name like ../../etc/cron.d/x escapes the destination directory, giving an attacker arbitrary file write from an untrusted upload.

rules.name: zipslip-node-concat-entry-write
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Never concatenate entry names into write paths. Resolve with path.resolve(dest, entry.path), assert startsWith(path.resolve(dest)+path.sep), reject symlink/absolute entries, then write.
rules.why: A file write/mkdir target is built by string-concatenating the destination with an archive entry name (dest + entry.path); string concat bypasses even path.join normalization and lets ../ or an absolute entry name write outside the destination directory.

rules.name: zipslip-node-pathjoin-entryname
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: After joining, verify the resolved path stays inside dest: const full = path.resolve(dest, name); if (!full.startsWith(path.resolve(dest)+path.sep)) throw. Prefer a vetted safe-join helper and skip symlink/absolute entries.
rules.why: A per-entry write path is built by joining the destination with an attacker-controlled archive entry name (entry.entryName/fileName/path) from an unzipper/tar/adm-zip loop; without a containment check the join resolves outside dest for names containing ../, enabling arbitrary file write.

rules.name: zipslip-php-ziparchive-extractto
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Validate entries before extracting: for each name, realpath(dir . '/' . $name) must str_starts_with the realpath of the destination; reject '..'/absolute names and symlink entries. Prefer per-entry extraction with an explicit containment check over whole-archive extractTo on untrusted input.
rules.why: ZipArchive::extractTo() and PharData::extractTo() unpack every entry into the target directory using in-archive names; PharData in particular does not defend against ../ entries, so extracting an untrusted archive can write files outside the destination. Allowing whitespace after -> catches spaced arrows without matching exportTo/extractToArray.

rules.name: zipslip-python-open-join-write
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Compute the joined path, canonicalize with os.path.realpath, and confirm it starts with the realpath of dest before opening for write; reject '..' and absolute entry names.
rules.why: Manual extraction opens a write-mode file at os.path.join(dest, <entry name>) inside a zip/tar loop; because the entry name is untrusted, a name with ../ or a leading slash makes os.path.join resolve outside dest, writing attacker-controlled bytes to an arbitrary path. Word boundaries keep the name tokens from matching safe identifiers such as dirname/basename/pathname.

rules.name: zipslip-python-tar-zip-extract-member
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Before extracting a member, build target = os.path.join(dest, member.name), resolve with os.path.realpath, and require it to start with the resolved dest; skip absolute names, '..', and symlink/hardlink members (or use tarfile filter='data').
rules.why: tar.extract(member,...) / zip.extract(name,...) writes a single member using its in-archive name; without validating the destination, a traversal name or link member escapes the target directory and writes to an arbitrary location.

rules.name: zipslip-python-tar-zip-extractall
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: On Python 3.12+ pass filter='data' (data_filter). Otherwise validate each member: os.path.realpath(os.path.join(dest, name)) must start with os.path.realpath(dest); reject absolute names, '..', and link members before extracting.
rules.why: tarfile/zipfile extractall() writes all members using their in-archive names; a member named ../../etc/passwd (or an absolute path, or a symlink member) is written outside the target directory, a classic arbitrary-write / TarSlip primitive.

rules.name: zipslip-ruby-zip-entry-name
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Compute dest_path = File.join(dest, entry.name), canonicalize with File.realpath/File.expand_path, and require it to start_with?(File.expand_path(dest) + File::SEPARATOR) before extracting; reject '..'/absolute names and skip symlink entries.
rules.why: rubyzip entry.extract(dest) and File.join(dest, entry.name) write using the untrusted entry.name; a name containing ../ escapes the destination, so extraction of a malicious zip yields an arbitrary file write. Word boundaries keep entry.extract/entry.name from matching entry_data/entryset.

rules.name: zipslip-symlink-entry-linkname
rules.message: Zip Slip / insecure archive extraction — an archive entry name escapes the destination, arbitrary file write (CWE-22/59).
rules.remediation: Resolve the symlink's final target against dest and require it to stay inside (realpath/EvalSymlinks then prefix check); reject absolute link targets and any target that traverses out of dest, or refuse to materialize symlink entries from untrusted archives entirely.
rules.why: A symlink is created from an untrusted archive entry's link target (member.linkname / header.Linkname / entry.getLinkName). An attacker can point the link at an absolute or ../ path (e.g. /etc or a parent dir) so a subsequent entry writes through the link, escaping the extraction directory - a link-following variant of zip slip.
